svg.text: Operational product · NASA/JPL OPERA
How OPERA DSWx-S1 turns Sentinel-1 VV + VH into a water map
Dynamic Surface Water eXtent from Sentinel-1 · 30 m · open data since 2024
Big idea:
No single clue is trusted: radar darkness in two polarisations is weighed against terrain and history.
Two echoes of one pulse
Sentinel-1 sends a vertically polarised
pulse and records two echoes: VV and VH.
OPERA's RTC product corrects both for
terrain on a 30 m grid; bursts are
mosaicked so a scene holds enough water
and land.
Threshold map from shore tiles
Only tiles with two clear humps that also
cross a known JRC shoreline are used.
Kittler–Illingworth gives each a
threshold; these are interpolated into a
map, for VV and for VH.
Turn every clue into a score
Fuzzy logic: dark VV, dark VH, flat
ground, low HAND and 'often water in the
past' each become a 0–1 water-likeness
score. Their average is the composite
score.
Grow water from sure seeds
Pixels scoring ≥ 0.8 are sure water.
Water spreads to neighbours scoring ≥
0.6, but only when connected to a seed;
isolated look-alikes stay out.
Remove dark land
Bare soil, sand or smooth fields can be
as dark as water. If land cover allows it
and both polarisations are very dark, the
pixel is ruled not-water.
Check water-body edges

g.text: pixels along each water body's edge

svg.text: Along a real shoreline, backscatter
splits into a water hump and a land hump.
Objects whose edge pixels show no such
split are removed as false alarms.
Find water under vegetation

g.text: VV bright, VH much weaker → high VV/VH
mapped only in wetland / vegetation classes

svg.text: Under plants, the pulse bounces water →
stem → satellite and returns bright,
mostly in VV. A high VV/VH ratio inside
vegetated land-cover classes is mapped as
inundated vegetation.
Mask and package
Pixels too high above drainage (HAND) or
in radar layover/shadow are flagged.
Results are cut into 30 m MGRS tiles with
four layers.
Sources: OPERA DSWx-S1/NI ATBD (JPL D-108763 Rev A, May 2024); DSWx-S1 product specification Rev A; metadata of DSWx-S1 tiles over Warren County, KY (Feb 2025).
Current product files name GLAD Global Land Cover 2020 (the ATBD names ESA WorldCover) and some different fuzzy ranges (e.g. HAND 0–15 m). Schematic illustration.
